newsitem.title: UK: London platinum fixed at highest since Nov 1996.
newsitem.headline: London platinum fixed at highest since Nov 1996.

text.p: Platinum was fixed at $377.00 per ounce on Wednesday, its highest fixing since November 27, 1996.
Palladium was fixed at $141.25, matching its recent high of February 13 this year, which was its highest fixing since March 27 last year.
Prices of the platinum group metals have soared this year since talks on export contracts between Russia and Japan were delayed late last year.
Russia is the world's largest supplier of palladium and second largest exporter of platinum and Japan is the biggest consumer of both metals.

They are produced at the giant Norilsk metallurgical plant in Arctic Siberia where cash problems and unpaid wages have led to threats of production disruptions. Itar-Tass news agency reported on Wednesday that workers at Norilsk may go on srike on March 15.
An official of the Russian export agency Almaz said this week that talks with Japan could start next month but industry sources said deliveries to Japan were unlikely before April.
